title: Regulating financial conglomerates
summary_en: When a single financial-services group combines banking, insurance, and asset management, regulating each silo separately may miss group-wide risk. Freixas, Lóránth and Morrison study optimal regulation of financial conglomerates and identify when entity-level vs. group-level supervision dominates. They show that group-level rules are warranted when intra-group capital flows substitute for arms-length funding, but become counter-productive when entities are genuinely separated, and they characterise the capital-requirement structure that minimises systemic risk in each case.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No primary dataset; the analysis is a contract-theoretic model of conglomerate regulation under intra-group capital mobility.
policy_relevance: Direct theoretical input for MNB and EU regulators (ECB / EBA, EIOPA) overseeing Hungarian and pan-European bancassurance groups (OTP, Allianz, Generali). The paper provides the analytical toolkit for deciding when group-level capital requirements add value over entity-level capital floors — a recurring question in Hungarian financial-conglomerate supervision and in EU CRD/Solvency II coordination.
